title: fix(plugin-detail): record:chatter.feed carries the affordance members, and says so (objectui#8934)
body:
Fixes #8934

**⚠️ Route changed. This PR now implements option 1 (close the implementation
gap). Its first revision did the opposite — it narrowed the published
description to match the implementation — and that direction was overturned.**

The maintainer principle it was overturned on, quoted verbatim and untranslated:

> 我们的项目以 objectstack 协议为准，文档应该以实际实现为准。协议不正确的应该先修改协议。

Ruling on the card: objectui#8934 comment `5617613810`. Contract review of the
first revision: `VERDICT: REWORK` at PR comment `5617990272`, adopted verbatim
by the dispatching seat at `5618030020`.

**Round 3** answers the incremental review at PR comment `5619284866`, which
passed the contract core — pipeline shape, both registered names, the inverted
pin with live controls, the protocol-true description, the `minor` level — and
left a narrow remainder: R1 (the tree claims two chatter surfaces are
identical, and they no longer are), R2 (the docs callout was silent on
objectui#8968), R3 (dispose of the stale console docblock), R4 (a wording nit).
All four are below; **no code path changed in round 3** — the only source edit
is the `feed` description losing one word.

## The measurement the new route rests on, re-derived here

`objectstack-ai/objectstack` HEAD `eabdd66f45f402eba0f8404a8a9de4a501fc83a6`,
`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` — read in this round, not inherited:

| reading | value |
| --- | --- |
| `RecordChatterProps` | `:1349`, a `strictObject` |
| its `feed` member | `:1366` — `feed: RecordActivityProps.optional().describe('Embedded activity feed configuration')`, under the docblock `/** Feed configuration (delegates to RecordActivityProps) */` |
| bound to | **both** names — `:2948` `'record:chatter': RecordChatterProps`, `:2962` `'record:discussion': RecordChatterProps`, deliberately the same schema object |
| `RecordActivityProps` | `:1248`, carrying `types` `:1267`, `filterMode` `:1271`, `showFilterToggle` `:1273`, `limit` `:1275`, `showCompleted` `:1277`, `unifiedTimeline` `:1279`, and the write-side members below them |

⇒ The protocol declares `feed` to be the full `record:activity` shape. ObjectUI
not applying the filter members on the chatter path was an **implementation
gap**, not a narrower contract, and "same shape as `record:activity`" was true
of the protocol all along.

**The declared defaults agree with the implementation's, exactly** — worth
stating because they are what makes this a behaviour change:
`limit: z.number().int().positive().default(20)` against
`DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT = 20`; `showCompleted: z.boolean().default(false)`
against `applyFeedConfig`'s `config.showCompleted !== true`;
`unifiedTimeline: z.boolean().default(true)` against un-mixing only on an
explicit `false`.

## What landed

**1. The pipeline.** `renderers/record-chatter.tsx` runs `applyFeedConfig`
before handing items to `RecordChatterPanel`, in `record-activity.tsx:219`'s
call shape — `applyFeedConfig(sourceItems, { types, showCompleted, unifiedTimeline }, pageSize)`
— and reads `limit` as the page window with the same `extraPages`-is-the-state
shape (`record-activity.tsx:159-160`). ⛔ No second calling convention.

`hasMore` / `onLoadMore` are wired to the panel's existing props in the same
change. Without that pair an authored `limit` would be a silent truncation
rather than the page size the spec's own description says it is
("Number of items to load per page").

**2. The description went back to the protocol's statement, not to its old
bytes.** It now reads:

> Activity-feed configuration nested inside the panel — the same shape as record:activity. The spec declares this key as RecordActivityProps (RecordChatterProps.feed), so its members are exactly the inputs record:activity declares; see that block for what each one does.

Same claim as the original sentence, plus the spec symbol it delegates to, so a
reader can check the claim instead of trusting it. ⛔ It says nothing about any
member not taking effect. The registration comment above it records why the
declaration is **not** narrowed to whatever the renderer happens to read.

**3. The `plugin-detail.mdx` callout is gone.** It documented the gap as if it
were the contract. Replaced with an `info` callout stating the delegation and
the two visible defaults, which is documentation following the implementation.

**4. The behaviour pin is inverted**, and renamed to match its subject:
`recordChatterFeedAffordanceOnly-8934.test.tsx` →
`recordChatterFeedMembersLive-8934.test.tsx`. 25 cases, all green.

## The pin, and what replaced the old control

The first revision asserted "a filter authored inside `feed` changes nothing".
The review is right that this was a **lock on option 1** — and the ablation in
that revision proved it, because wiring the pipeline in turned exactly those
cases red. Inverted:

- **FILTER legs (new direction)** — `showCompleted`, `types`,
  `unifiedTimeline` and `limit` each move the rendered panel, run against both
  names.
- **KEEP-LEG, one per member** — every value that removes a row is paired with
  a value of the *same* member that keeps it, so "the row is gone" is never
  satisfiable by a panel rendering nothing.
- **AGREEMENT** — the ids the panel renders are computed in the test from
  `applyFeedConfig` for the same authored config, so the pin names *which*
  pipeline ran rather than only that something moved. `applyFeedConfig` is no
  longer a control here; it is the subject, which is exactly why the three legs
  above exist.
- **UNDECLARED-KEY** — a key the shape does not declare, authored in the same
  position, moves nothing. Without it every leg above is satisfiable by a panel
  reacting to the mere presence of a `feed` object.
- **DEFAULTS CONTROL** — with no `feed` authored at all the panel renders
  `['c-1','f-1','c-2']`, equal to `applyFeedConfig(ITEMS, {})`, so "no config"
  is a reading and not an empty panel.
- **kept, route-independent** — the five affordance legs and the
  `showSubscriptionToggle` pin on `RecordActivityTimeline`.
- **R5 adopted** — the per-name cases now resolve the renderer through
  `ComponentRegistry.get(blockName)` instead of taking the name as a label
  while always rendering the imported symbol. The imported symbol keeps one
  case of its own as the control that the lookup resolves to this module.

**Ablation (one-shot, restored, re-run against the final head).** Reverting the
one line `items={applied.items}` to the pre-fix raw items turns **11 of 25**
cases red — the four filter legs on both names, both AGREEMENT legs and the
defaults control — while the affordance legs, the subscription pin, the
undeclared-key control and the declaration legs stay green. That partition is
the claim: the new legs measure the pipeline, the kept legs do not depend on it.
Mutation proved on disk first (original marker 1 → 0, injected marker 1, blob
`4dde2ce8` → `4c36522e`); restored by blob equality back to `4dde2ce8` with an
empty `git diff HEAD` for that path.

## Behaviour change, stated plainly — and which surfaces it reaches

⚠️ **Scoped in round 3**, because the first wording was over-broad. This reaches
an **authored `record:chatter` / `record:discussion` block**, and every
synthesized default page (`synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts:880-883` emits
`record:discussion`) — the surfaces that render through
`RecordChatterRenderer`. It does **not** reach the panel the host auto-appends
when a page omits a discussion block: `app-shell`
`RecordDetailView.tsx:2549` mounts `RecordChatterPanel` directly with raw items
(that file has 0 occurrences of `applyFeedConfig`, `hasMore` and `onLoadMore`),
so it is unchanged. See R1 below.

On the surfaces it does reach, they now inherit `record:activity`'s defaults for
the members they had been ignoring:

- **completed activities (feed type `task`) are no longer rendered** unless the
  block authors `feed: { showCompleted: true }`;
- **a feed longer than 20 items now pages**, with a "Load more" control, rather
  than rendering whole. Nothing is dropped; the window grows by `limit` per
  click.

`types` and `unifiedTimeline` change nothing unless authored.

## Not closed here

`filterMode` and `enableMentions` are also members of the declared shape and are
still unread on this path: `RecordActivityTimeline` takes `filterMode` as a
component **prop** (`:187`, `:212`), never off `config`, and the chatter path's
mentions come from the host context's `mentionSuggestions`. `applyFeedConfig`
covers the four filter members only, so this change does **not** make either
live — measured, not assumed. Tracked as objectui#8968. The host fallback panel
is tracked as objectui#8983.

## Round 3 — the review's remainder

**R1 — took route (b), at the dispatching seat's decision.** ⛔ Not (a): routing
the host fallback through the same pipeline is a further behaviour change on
authored pages that omit a discussion node, which this card's ruling does not
authorize. Instead:

- **Filed objectui#8983** for the divergence, unassigned and ungraded, carrying
  a reproducible probe (deleted, not committed) that mounts the two surfaces
  side by side on the identical feed:

  | feed | host fallback | authored / synthesized block |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 3 comments + 1 `task` row | 4 rows, Load more ×0 | 3 rows, Load more ×0 |
  | 25 comments | 25 rows, Load more ×0 | 20 rows, Load more ×1 |
  | **CONTROL** — 3 comments, no `task` | 3 rows, Load more ×0 | 3 rows, Load more ×0 |

  The control row is what makes the other two a measurement rather than a
  harness in which the two could never have agreed.

- **Rewrote the false sentence.** `renderers/record-chatter.tsx` claimed its
  defaults matched the host fallback "so an author-placed `record:discussion`
  looks identical to the fallback the host injects when no component is
  present". The affordance defaults still match; the rendered feed does not.
  The comment now says exactly that, quotes what it used to say, carries the
  measured rows, points at objectui#8983 and forbids restoring the old sentence
  before the divergence is closed.

- **Scoped the claim** in the PR body (above), the changeset and the docs
  callout.

**R2 — the callout carries the clause the other files had.**
`content/docs/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx` now names the two members this path
still does not read (`filterMode`, `enableMentions`, objectui#8968) and the
fallback panel that does not run the pipeline (objectui#8983). Docs follow the
implementation.

**R3 — took disposition A on the stale console docblock.**
`apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` had a paragraph
still describing the filter members as inert inside `feed` and quoting the
description this branch replaced. Corrected in place. ⛔ Comment only — no
assertion in that file reads the string (re-verified), and that file's ledger,
ceiling and exemption tables are untouched. The paragraph is eight lines, not
the seven the review cited: its opening clause ("The `feed` pin records a
LIMIT…") is the subject of the false sentence, and leaving it would have made
the paragraph contradict itself.

**R4 — nit taken.** "so its members are **exactly** the inputs record:activity
declares" → "so its members are the inputs record:activity declares". The spec
shape also carries `aria`, which `record:activity`'s registration does not list,
so "exactly" invited a parity reading to disagree. The registration comment
records that as one more reason the delegation, rather than a re-listing, is the
honest statement.

## Changeset

Re-levelled `patch` → **`minor`**. `patch` was right for a description-only
edit and is wrong for this: it changes what shipped pages render. This
repository never declares `major` (the fixed release group would drag every
package off `@objectstack`'s cadence), and its own breaking-semantics changes
are `minor` with the breakage spelled out in the notes — which is what the two
bullets above are.

## Verification

Every exit code captured into a file **before** any pipe.

| run | result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' build` | exit 0 — run first, or `type-check` is a wall of pre-existing `TS2307` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` | exit 0 — **160 files, 1498 tests passed** |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/ packages/app-shell/src/utils/` | exit 0 — **446 files, 4515 passed, 1 skipped** |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` on the three console files that name these blocks — `record-block-record-reach.test.tsx`, `public-contract.test.ts`, `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` | exit 0 — **3 files, 230 tests passed** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` | exit 0 — log echoes the script name and both legs (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail lint` | **exit 0** — log echoes the script name; the only line carrying the literal word `error` is `✖ 1000 problems (0 errors, 1000 warnings)` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — 4 published source files changed, 1 changeset declared |
| `pnpm changeset:check` | exit 0 — fixed group OK, no `major` |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | exit 0 (7166 files) + a manual scan of the six diff files |
| `check:doc-types` / `check:doc-fences` / `check-doc-links` / `check-docs-route-eager-closure` | exit 0 each |

The app-shell and console suites are run because this change moves a **rendered
result** on a published block, so import-side coverage is owed rather than
optional.

**Round 3 re-runs**, after the four edits above (three of which are comments and
one is a description string; no code path moved):

| run | result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` | exit 0 — 160 files, 1498 tests |
| `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` | exit 0 — 198 tests |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` | exit 0 — **after** `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build`; without that closure it is exit 2 with 159 `TS2307`/`TS2882` module-resolution errors, two of which name the file edited here at lines 296-297 and are unrelated to the edit at 2765 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail lint` | exit 0 — `✖ 1000 problems (0 errors, 1000 warnings)` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console lint` | exit 0 — `✖ 212 problems (0 errors, 212 warnings)`. Two other lines carry the literal word `error`; both are source context printed inside a warning (`setStatus('error')`, a variable named `error`), not diagnostics |
| changeset presence / `changeset:check` / control-bytes / four docs gates | exit 0 each |

Warnings went 1004 → **1000** for the package, and the one
`Compilation Skipped` advisory this change first introduced (React Compiler
could not preserve the manual memoization of `handleLoadMore` with an empty
dependency list) is gone: the dependency array names the stable setter, with a
comment recording the one-token deviation from `record-activity.tsx:233`.

## 验收备注

- **Resolved in round 3, disposition A:** the stale docblock in
  `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` is corrected
  here. The dispatching seat lifted the file-surface hold for that paragraph
  only, having measured that objectui#8071 has no slice PR open. Nothing else in
  that file is touched.
- `RecordChatterComponentProps.feed?: RecordActivityComponentProps`
  (`packages/types/src/record-components.ts:257`, not `:253` as the first
  revision's report said) stays untouched, and the reason is the contract one
  the review named, not branch coordination: it is the **protocol's twin** and
  matches `component.zod.ts:1366`. Narrowing it locally is what the ruling
  refuses.
- `record:chatter` is deliberately **not** a public block
  (`packages/core/src/registry/public-blocks.ts:56-61`), so this description
  reaches `sdui.manifest.json` under `record:discussion` only; `record:chatter`
  reaches an author through the TS type and `ComponentRegistry.getConfig`. The
  first revision's "ships to `sdui.manifest.json`" was half true — adopted from
  review item R5.

Session: `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`. PR stays **draft**.
